title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Code — latest changelog adds EndConversation tool + progress heartbeats and makes /verify and /code-review invoke-only, with tighter permission scoping
bullets.summary: The newest Claude Code release (checked this fire, fresher than the Jul-18 /fork-background entry the morning cited) is a broad stability-and-safety pass: an EndConversation tool (no-op in background forks), a periodic progress heartbeat for long-running tool calls that previously went silent, tighter permission checks, and safer Bash/PowerShell handling. Two changes lead: /verify and /code-review now run only when invoked directly (Claude no longer fires them on its own), and the single-segment dir/** allow-rule bug is fixed so Edit(src/**) no longer auto-approves writes to nested dir/ directories anywhere in the tree.
bullets.how: The invoke-only change for /verify and /code-review is confirmed live in this very session's tooling — first-hand provenance, not a vendor-page claim — and the tightened dir/** scoping is a real safety improvement for our fan-out subagent jobs; progress heartbeats close the 'long job went silent' gap on scans like this one. Audit our permission allow-rules against the new scoping before the next big fleet run.

bullets.title: Gemini Omni Flash lands in Google Vids (Jul 17) — conversational video editing + personal avatars from a text prompt
bullets.summary: Google put Omni Flash inside Google Vids on Jul 17: edit existing video with plain-text prompts and generate new clips with an avatar that looks and sounds like you. The underlying model (developer API since Jun 30) takes any mix of text/image/audio/video in and outputs physics-aware video at $0.10 per second, with conversational editing as its differentiator versus every other API video model. New this fire: Revid.ai shipped a video-production MCP Jul 16 (script-to-video, schedule_publish/publish_now) — a closer-to-B9S, agent-callable bench candidate, parked for the same video bench.
bullets.how: Squarely on Brand 9 Signs' surface (short-form video for signage clients, social cuts) and on Vector's remit in The Construct, but we already route generative video/image through the Higgsfield MCP fleet. Worth one bench: does conversational text-prompt editing at $0.10/sec beat our current pipeline on a real B9S social cut, or is it a second vendor we don't need? Test, don't adopt on a launch post.

bullets.title: MCP specification 2026-07-28 goes final in 9 days — the largest breaking revision since launch (carried)
bullets.summary: The maintainers' RC stands: the core goes stateless (the initialize/initialized handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header are removed; any request can land on any instance), Streamable HTTP now requires Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name routing headers, list/read results carry ttlMs and cacheScope, authorization aligns to OAuth/OpenID Connect, and the missing-resource error moves from custom -32002 to standard -32602. SDK betas (Python v2 FastMCP->MCPServer; TypeScript v2 ESM-only, split into server/client packages; Go v1.7.0-pre.1; C# 2.0.0-preview.1) are out now.
bullets.how: Every MCP server The Construct runs is on the far side of a breaking change in 9 days. Two exposures remain live: any code matching the literal -32002, and any skill assuming session-scoped state the transport will no longer carry. The /doctor pass is the vehicle — produce the unused-server list and the Jul-28 migration inventory in one sitting, before the deadline, not on Jul 29.

bullets.title: arXiv 'Context Engineering: From Prompts to Corporate Multi-Agent Architecture' — five context-quality criteria for a governed fleet
bullets.summary: The paper reframes context management for enterprise agent fleets around five quality criteria — relevance, sufficiency, isolation, economy, provenance — and introduces 'intent engineering': encoding organizational goals, values, and trade-off hierarchies into the agent infrastructure itself rather than into individual prompts.
bullets.how: A clean vocabulary for what The Construct already does ad hoc across its skill/MCP fleet; 'economy' and 'provenance' map exactly onto the two things this scan keeps relearning (context cost of unused servers; never letting an unconfirmed detail age into fact). A framework to borrow for the installed-skills registry and memory system, read against our CLAUDE.md governance and the /doctor output, not a tool to install.

praxis_lesson: The clean second-fire move is to let the freshest primary source overwrite the morning's placeholder: the 06:01 brief cited the Jul-18 /fork changelog, but the newest Claude Code release is a safety pass whose most load-bearing change — /verify and /code-review now invoke-only — is confirmable live in this session's own tooling, so it replaces a vendor-page claim with a first-hand fact. Bank what you can verify first-hand, and still run one /doctor pass that does double duty: the unused-MCP-server list and the Jul-28 migration inventory, before the deadline.
